## PII TTL — recent_messages scrub (FIX-1, 2026-08-27)

**What:** every day at 04:00 this second branch clears `conversations.recent_messages` on rows whose
`last_updated` is older than **30 days**.

**Why the row is KEPT, not deleted:** deleting the row would (a) silently release a `stage='handoff'`
lock — a handed-off customer would start getting bot replies again with nobody deciding that — and
(b) drop `cancel_target_id`/`confirm_turn`. Row deletion is a separate decision (UX-ARCHITECTURE §9 K2).

**Honest scope:** this expires message CONTENT. `sender_key` (a phone number on whatsapp) survives for
the row's lifetime. Do NOT describe this as "PII TTL solved".

## Purge failures now reach a human (FIX-1)

This workflow had **no alert at all**: if the dedupe purge or the PII scrub broke, cleaning just
silently stopped. Same silent-failure class as `cancel_mirror_failed`.

**Two collectors, on purpose.** An n8n error item carries only `{message, error}` — never the node
that failed. One collector would say "purge broke" without saying WHICH cleanup stopped, so the
branch is identified by **topology**: `Purge Error (processed)` vs `Purge Error (PII)`. Both fan into one composer, and the
throttle key carries the branch (`purge_error:<branch>`).

**Drill-corrected (exec 1631):** the first build used ONE global throttle key. n8n runs a node once per
INCOMING CONNECTION, not once with merged inputs — so run#0 (processed) alerted and run#1 (PII) hit the
key it had just set and returned `[]`. The PII failure was **swallowed** — the exact thing the two
collectors exist to prevent. Keying on class+branch makes them independent.

**Config:** `Load Config (Purge)` carries `ownerAlert` and sits on the main path so it always runs.
Its `enabled`/`throttleMinutes` MUST match main + reminders — asserted by
`scripts/check-cancel-validation-parity.py`. A kill-switch that silences only some alerts is broken.

**Not covered (honest):** the two Code nodes (`Compute Purge Cutoff`, `Compute PII Cutoff`) are not
wrapped — a throw there fails the execution, visible in n8n's log but not on Telegram. Same scope as
the reminders workflow.

## leads TTL — the branch the public deploy is GATED on
A stranger can type a real phone number into the public demo's lead capture (`dryRun=false`, D-11) and `leads` had no expiry at all. Cutoff comes from `leadsRetentionDays` in config — **absent = delete nothing and alert**.

⚠ **The CANDIDATE CAP is the load-bearing node**, not the delete: `min(200, 20% of the table)`. Without it one wrong cutoff costs the table; with it, one Telegram message.
⚠ **CORRECTED BY A DRILL (exec 2764).** This note first said rows with an EMPTY `created_at` "never match and never expire". The OPPOSITE is true: Airtable sorts a blank below any string, so `{created_at} < cutoff` MATCHED all 3 blank rows and they would have been deleted on every run. The filter now carries `{created_at} != ""`, and blank rows are REPORTED rather than deleted — their age is unknown, and deleting a row of unknown age is the irreversible choice. Who owns them is an OPEN item.
